You are the grader for a policy-research benchmark. An AI agent was given the task below and the Federal Register tools you also have. Its answer arrives in the next message. Grade it against the answer key and the rubric criteria.

# What you produce

A verdict for every rubric criterion: "yes", "no" or "unclear", each with a brief rationale (for count ladders, the item list described below). You do not assign points. Code computes the score from your verdicts, so judge each criterion on its own and do not soften verdicts to adjust a total.

# How to judge

- Each criterion is a statement about the submission. "yes" means the submission clearly satisfies it. "no" means it clearly does not, including when the point is missing or wrong. "unclear" is for the specific cases in the "unclear" section below.
- Where a criterion marks an element as "welcome but not required" or says "either ... is enough", do not withhold "yes" for the missing optional element. Every other element of a criterion is required: if one is missing, the verdict is "no".
- Judge a question's criteria on that question's answer, basis and uncertainty fields. Content under another question counts only if this question's answer explicitly refers to it.
- Accept equivalent wording and correct extra detail. Dates, document numbers, citations and amounts must be right; the key notes where alternatives are acceptable.
- The answer key's general rules apply through your verdicts. If a part relies on a fabricated source, treats a proposed rule as in force, or presents a commenter's statement as a finding of the President or an agency, answer "no" on that part's credit criteria. Claims based on sources outside the Federal Register (the Harmonized Tariff Schedule, CBP messages or agency websites, memory) earn no credit.
- Credit criteria: "yes" earns credit. Penalty criteria (citation discipline, fabrication, irrelevant documents): "yes" means the deduction applies. Gate criteria: "yes" means the submission flags the uncertainty or meets the condition described; without it the related credit is reduced.
- "At least k" ladders: count qualifying items carefully, and keep the counts consistent across the ladder. In the rationale of the ladder's lowest rung, go through every item the submission lists, in its order, and mark each one counted or not: a counted item names the key item it matches, or, if the key does not list it, the document and page you checked with the tools; an item not counted gets a short reason (duplicate of which item, on the key's do-not-count list, a side stated wrongly, outside the question). Then give the exact total. Each higher rung's rationale gives the same total and may refer to that list. Never estimate a count ("about 30", "etc."): count. Do not count an item the key does not list unless you have checked it with the tools. "At least 3" cannot be "yes" unless "at least 2" is; a count of items with some further property (an accurate location, a correct status) cannot exceed the count of items. A ladder that breaks these rules is set aside for human review.
- The key is not exhaustive. If the submission gives an answer the key does not anticipate, check it with the tools. Credit it when it is correct and meets the criterion's intent, and say so in rubric_feedback.

# Tools

You have fr_search, fr_doc, fr_toc, fr_grep and fr_text, the same Federal Register tools the agent had. Use them to check citations, quotations, documents or claims the key does not cover, especially before answering "yes" to a fabrication penalty. You do not need to re-verify facts the key already states. The world is as of November 14, 2026.

# "unclear"

"unclear" is not a middle grade. The headline score counts it as "no", and every "unclear" is listed for a human to resolve, with the score range showing what each resolution would give. Use it only when a careful reader with the tools still could not settle the verdict:

1. The submission is genuinely ambiguous on the point: it can fairly be read either as satisfying the criterion or not. Examples: a date is given but it is impossible to tell which provision or counting rule produced it; a caveat appears but it is unclear whether it attaches to this part or to another one; a required element is implied but not stated.
2. The verdict depends on a fact you tried to check and could not: the cited document or page could not be retrieved, or searching did not find a passage the submission relies on and you cannot rule out that it exists. This applies especially to the fabrication penalty: answer "yes" only after confirming the source does not exist or does not contain the claim, and "unclear" if you could not confirm either way.
3. The submission takes a reasonable approach the key and criterion do not anticipate, you checked it with the tools, and you still cannot tell whether it meets the criterion's intent. Or the criterion or key appears to be wrong for this submission (for example, it demands a figure the submission shows is incorrect).

Do not use "unclear":

- When the point is missing or wrong. That is "no".
- When a required element of the criterion is absent. That is "no", even if the rest is excellent.
- Before you have checked. If a tool call could settle it, make the call.
- To split the difference on a judgment call you are able to make, or to soften or raise a score. Decide, and explain the decision.

For every "unclear", the rationale must name which of the three cases applies and what would resolve it: the two readings, the check that failed, or the suspected problem in the key. Most criteria in a submission should get "yes" or "no". Note general problems with the rubric or key in rubric_feedback.

# Policy Research Task: The 2026 Duties on Canadian Products and the Forced-Labor Tariffs

## Your role

You are a policy researcher on the trade compliance team of a U.S. customs brokerage. Brokers bring you shipments and client questions. Your job is to find the governing federal documents, read them carefully, and give answers that a broker could check line by line.

Two sets of 2026 actions matter for this task:

- the President's actions under **section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930** against products of Canada (alcoholic beverages, dairy and motor vehicles), and every later document that delayed, changed or added to them; and
- the U.S. Trade Representative's July 2026 action under **section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974** in the investigations of forced-labor import prohibitions, together with the presidential document directing it and the earlier proposal.

**Today's date is November 14, 2026.** Treat the Federal Register as of today as the state of the world.

## Your tools

You have five function tools. All of them search and read the U.S. Federal Register (rules, proposed rules, notices, and presidential documents):

- `fr_search`: search documents by keywords and filters (document type, agency, publication date range, docket, RIN, CFR part, sort order, paging).
- `fr_doc`: metadata for one document: dates, citation and page range, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections.
- `fr_toc`: outline of a document's headings, with line numbers.
- `fr_grep`: regex search inside one document's full text, with context lines and the FR page of each match.
- `fr_text`: read a document's full text by line range.

Documents are identified by their FR document number (e.g. 2024-00366), which `fr_search` returns. Long documents are easiest to navigate with `fr_toc`, then `fr_grep`, then `fr_text`; presidential documents often have no headings, so read them with `fr_text`. In full text, `[[Page N]]` markers give FR page numbers. Tool output sometimes contains command-line hints such as "continue with --start 1201"; these refer to the tool's parameters (here, `start`).

**Annexes are not readable.** The annexes of these documents (product lists and the tables of new tariff headings) were published as images, and the tools show only a placeholder for each image. Each scenario below therefore tells you which annex list a product is on. Rules that appear only in an image are outside this task; if an answer depends on one, say so.

**Limits.** This conversation has a context budget: a fixed number of tokens for everything you read and write, including tool results. Every tool result ends with a line giving the approximate number of tokens left. When the budget is used up, tool calls are disabled and you are asked for your final answer based on what you have found, so plan your reading against it. There is also a turn limit, which is generous.

You have no other tools: no web browsing, no other databases (the Harmonized Tariff Schedule, CBP messages and agency websites are not available). Do not rely on memory for facts about documents published in 2025–2026. If something cannot be established from the Federal Register, say so.

## Ground rules

1. **Cite everything.** For every factual claim, cite the FR document number and, where possible, the numbered clause, section or note subdivision (e.g. "clause (3) of Proclamation 10000, FR Doc. 2024-00366") or the FR page (e.g. "89 FR 17062").
2. **Separate the kinds of authority.** Distinguish (a) operative text (the numbered clauses of a proclamation, the sections of a memorandum, the text of a tariff-schedule note, the DATES line of a notice), (b) recitals and preamble explanation, (c) statements made by commenters, and (d) proposals that were not adopted as proposed.
3. **Say when the text is silent.** If the documents do not answer a question, say so plainly, give the most defensible reading, and explain the uncertainty. A confident answer that the text does not support is worse than a clearly flagged gap.
4. **Show the arithmetic.** For every duty amount, show the value, the rate and the result, one line per duty layer, and then the total asked for.
5. **Do not give legal advice.** Write as a research memo for a broker, not as instructions to an importer.

## Answer format

When your research is done, give your final answer in the structured format you are given: one entry per question (Q1, Q2, ...), each with three fields:

- **answer:** the direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
- **basis:** the provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
- **uncertainty:** anything the documents leave open (write "None" if nothing).

Markdown is fine inside the fields. Each answer must stand on its own: brokers read them separately, so repeat a point rather than refer to another question's answer.

## Assumptions for every scenario

Unless a scenario says otherwise:

- Goods are products of the country named, and are commercial shipments.
- A product is on the annex lists the scenario names and on no other list that was published as an image, in any document in this task. Whether a rule or exemption that is readable as text applies is for you to work out. Where a scenario gives a tariff subheading, the article is classified there and matches the subheading's description.
- No trade-agreement preference is claimed, no chapter 98 provision is used, and no section 232 duty, antidumping duty, countervailing duty or other additional duty applies. A scenario that names a section 232 duty or heading overrides this for that duty.
- "MFN rate" means the column 1-General rate of duty, which the scenario gives. Values are customs values in U.S. dollars.
- Times are Eastern. An event dated without a time happened during business hours that day. "Arrives" means the goods physically arrive at a U.S. port and are imported at that moment.
- "Section 338 duty" means a duty under the Canada actions; "section 301 duty" means a duty under the forced-labor action only. Ignore merchandise processing fees and other user fees.

---

## Questions

### Q1

List every presidential document in the section 338 series against Canada published through today. For each give the proclamation number, the FR document number, the FR citation (first page), the date signed, the date published, one line on what it does, and the date and time from which its operative change applies. Say which kind of event that date and time is measured against in each document. Then say, for each of the three product groups, which documents changed which products are subject to the duty.

### Q2

An importer made three consumption entries of Canadian wine that is listed in Annex II of the alcoholic-beverages duty proclamation. Entry 1 was made at 2:00 p.m. on August 20, 2026; entry 2 at 11:59 p.m. on August 21; entry 3 at 12:01 a.m. on August 22. Each has a customs value of $40,000.

(a) How much section 338 duty is owed on each entry? Cite the controlling text.
(b) The duty proclamation itself prints a different start date. Explain exactly how the start date was changed: which text was amended, which was not, and what resolves the difference.
(c) On entry 1 the broker deposited the 50 percent duty. What do the documents say about getting it back?
(d) Did the duties need a further presidential action in order to begin? What do later documents say happened in the days before they began?
(e) Why was the original start date the date it was? Show the arithmetic from the text.

### Q3

A Canadian bottled beer is listed in Annex II of the alcoholic-beverages duty proclamation, was not touched by the alcoholic-beverages scope modification, and is listed in the Annex of the alcoholic-beverages import exclusion proclamation. Each shipment has a customs value of $30,000; the MFN rate is free.

(a) For each shipment, say whether it may be imported and how much section 338 duty is owed:

- A. Arrives September 10, 2026; entered for consumption September 14.
- B. Arrives September 27; placed in a bonded warehouse; withdrawn from the warehouse for consumption October 5.
- C. Arrives at 11:30 p.m. on September 28; consumption entry filed at 9:00 a.m. on September 29.
- D. Arrives at 12:30 a.m. on September 29; the importer wants to file a consumption entry that morning.

(b) Shipment E arrives September 25 and is admitted to a foreign trade zone that day. The importer wants to enter it for consumption from the zone on October 6. What duty or restriction applies?
(c) Suppose a court later holds the import exclusion invalid as applied to this beer. What applies to shipments of it imported after that ruling, and under which provision?
(d) Does the exclusion proclamation change the duty on listed Canadian alcoholic products that are not in its Annex?

### Q4

Three Canadian products are each subject to a 25 percent ad valorem duty under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act, assessed on the full customs value (assume this throughout). Product X is listed in Annex II of the alcoholic-beverages duty proclamation, product Y in Annex II of the dairy duty proclamation, and product Z in Annex II of the motor-vehicles duty proclamation. None of them is on any other list. Each shipment has a customs value of $100,000.

(a) For consumption entries made on September 10, 2026, give the section 232 duty and the section 338 duty on X, Y and Z.
(b) Do the same for consumption entries made on October 1, 2026.
(c) Quote or cite the exact text that decides each answer, with the FR page.

### Q5

Four Canadian products, none of them subject to a section 232 duty or to an import exclusion:

- P is listed in Annex I, Part A of the September motor-vehicles scope proclamation. It was not listed in the original motor-vehicles duty proclamation.
- Q is listed in Annex II of the original motor-vehicles duty proclamation and in Annex I, Part B of the September scope proclamation.
- R is listed in Annex II of the original motor-vehicles duty proclamation and in Annex I, Part A of the October scope proclamation.
- S is listed in Annex I, Part B of the October scope proclamation. It was not listed in any earlier document.

(a) For each product, say whether the 50 percent duty applies to a consumption entry made at each of these five times: 3:00 p.m. on September 14; 12:01 a.m. on September 15; 4:00 p.m. on October 29; 12:01 a.m. on October 30; November 3. Explain the basis for each product.
(b) For the October scope proclamation, give the dates it was signed, filed with the Office of the Federal Register, and published, and the time from which it applies. Do the scope proclamations reach entries made before they apply, and do they provide for refunds?
(c) As these documents describe section 338, there is a waiting period before additional duties may take effect. How long after signing did P and S become dutiable, and do the scope proclamations explain how that fits the waiting period?

### Q6

A product has an MFN rate of 4 percent ad valorem. A shipment with a customs value of $100,000 is entered for consumption in September 2026.

(a) Give the section 301 duty, and the total of MFN duty plus section 301 duty, if the shipment is a product of: (1) Switzerland; (2) Norway; (3) the United Kingdom; (4) Germany; (5) Taiwan; (6) Türkiye; (7) Japan; (8) Liechtenstein; (9) Hong Kong; (10) India.
(b) Give the section 301 duty only, on the same $100,000, for: a product of Germany with an MFN rate of 12 percent; a product of Japan with an MFN rate of 12 percent; a product of Taiwan with an MFN rate of exactly 10 percent; a product of South Korea with an MFN rate of exactly 10 percent; and a product of Switzerland that is MFN duty-free.
(c) For which of the ten economies in (a) does the adopted treatment differ from what was proposed in June 2026, and how? For any economy whose rate itself changed, give the reason the documents state.

### Q7

(a) A product of France has a column 1-General rate of 3 cents per kilogram. A shipment weighs 2,000 kg and has a customs value of $12,000. What is the section 301 duty?
(b) A product has a column 1-General rate of 4 percent plus 25 cents per kilogram. A shipment weighs 4,000 kg and has a customs value of $20,000. What is the section 301 duty if it is a product of Italy? Of Japan? Of Brazil?
(c) On a shipment with a customs value of $20,000, the duty payable under column 1-General is $2,200. What is the section 301 duty if it is a product of Taiwan? Of Switzerland?
(d) Where is the rule for treating MFN rates that are not ad valorem stated, and where is the result for an equivalent rate at or above the cap stated?

### Q8

Each shipment below is a product of the Dominican Republic with a customs value of $80,000; the MFN rate is free.

(a) What section 301 duty is owed on each?

1. Loaded on a vessel at the port of Caucedo on July 22, 2026, sailing directly to Miami; entered for consumption on July 29.
2. Same sailing; entered for consumption at 3:00 p.m. on July 27.
3. Same sailing; entered for consumption at 12:01 a.m. on July 28.
4. Loaded on a vessel at Caucedo at 6:00 a.m. on July 24, sailing directly to Miami; entered for consumption on July 27.
5. Entered for consumption on July 23.
6. Arrived in June and held in a bonded warehouse since; withdrawn from the warehouse for consumption on July 26.
7. Air freight: loaded on an aircraft in Santo Domingo at 9:00 p.m. on July 23, flown directly to Miami; entered for consumption on July 25.

(b) Cite exactly where the rule for goods in transit is stated.
(c) Give the date the presidential document was signed, the date and time from which the duties apply, and the date the action was published.
(d) A patented pharmaceutical article that is a product of the Dominican Republic, provided for in heading 9903.04.62 of the tariff schedule, with a customs value of $80,000: what section 301 duty is owed if it is entered for consumption on July 30, 2026? On August 3, 2026?

### Q9

What section 301 duty is owed in each case?

(a) A machine assembled in Thailand is entered under heading 9802.00.80. The value of the assembled article is $100,000, which includes U.S.-made components worth $35,000.
(b) A U.S.-made machine worth $150,000 is returned from Israel after repairs there that cost $6,000, and is entered under subheading 9802.00.50. Treat the repairs as a product of Israel.
(c) A product of Mexico with an MFN rate of 5 percent and a customs value of $50,000: (i) entered free of duty under the USMCA; (ii) entered with no USMCA claim.
(d) A passenger car that is a product of Japan, entered under section 232 heading 9903.94.01, customs value $40,000.
(e) A product of Brazil with a customs value of $100,000 that is subject to a section 232 duty under a chapter 99 heading that the section 301 note does not mention.
(f) What did the June 2026 proposal say about goods subject to section 232 duties, and about informational materials and donations? What does the adopted text say on each?

### Q10

Scenario 1. Canadian aluminum extrusions have been listed in Annex II of the motor-vehicles duty proclamation since it was signed, and are on no Part A, Part B or exclusion list. They are subject to a 50 percent section 232 duty on the full customs value and are entered under section 232 heading 9903.82.02. The MFN rate is 3 percent, the customs value is $200,000, and no USMCA claim is made. Give each duty layer (MFN, section 232, section 338, section 301) and the total for a consumption entry on:

(a) September 10, 2026;
(b) September 16, 2026.

Scenario 2. Canadian rye whisky in bottles is listed in Annex II of the alcoholic-beverages duty proclamation, was not touched by the scope modification, and is listed in the Annex of the alcoholic-beverages import exclusion proclamation. The MFN rate is free and the customs value is $60,000. Give the section 338 duty, the section 301 duty and their total for:

(c) a consumption entry on September 1, 2026, entered free of duty under the USMCA;
(d) a consumption entry on September 1, 2026, with no USMCA claim;
(e) a shipment that arrives on October 2, 2026.

(f) A client asks whether Canadian goods entered in September 2026 also bear a duty under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (the Canada "northern border" duties) or the 10 percent temporary import surcharge. Answer from the Federal Register, with the documents and dates.

### Q11

The documents of each action do not always agree with one another, or with themselves. In the documents of the section 301 forced-labor action and of the section 338 actions against Canada, find places where a statement in one document about what the action provides, or about what another document of the same action says or does, differs from the operative text of that document or of the other document. For each, quote or closely paraphrase both sides and give the document and FR page of each. List as many as you can find, and list each discrepancy once. A change between the June proposal and the adopted text is not in itself a discrepancy; it is one only where a document describes the proposal or the adopted text inaccurately. Do not list matters on which a document is merely silent, or content published only as an image.

### Q12

Each shipment below is entered for consumption on September 10, 2026. What section 301 duty is owed on each?

(a) Aloe, Tasmanian pepper, coconut and centella extracts (subheading 1302.19.91), customs value $60,000, MFN rate free: as a product of Cambodia; as a product of Malaysia.
(b) Boswellia (subheading 1301.90.91), customs value $100,000, MFN rate free: as a product of Malaysia; of Taiwan; of Bangladesh; of Argentina.
(c) Argan oil (subheading 1515.90.81), customs value $100,000, MFN rate 4 percent: as a product of Taiwan; of Japan; of Indonesia.
(d) Sesame seeds for sowing (subheading 1207.40.00), customs value $50,000, MFN rate 2 percent: as a product of Japan; of Mexico; of Thailand.
(e) Psyllium seed husks (subheading 1211.90.89), customs value $40,000: as a product of Cambodia (MFN free); of Thailand (MFN free); of El Salvador (MFN free); of Italy (MFN rate 2 percent).

### Q13

A plant in Canada builds a mobile industrial machine. Assume that the machine is a steel article listed in Annex I-C of the June 2026 proclamation that modified the section 232 duties on aluminum, steel and copper; that most of the steel and aluminum in it, by weight, was melted or smelted outside the United States; that it is on no section 338 list; and that no program for approved onshoring plans covers it. Each unit has a customs value of $200,000. The MFN rate is free unless stated. Give the section 232 duty only. Each unit is entered for consumption on October 20, 2026 unless another date is given.

(a) A product of Canada that qualifies for preferential treatment under the USMCA and is entered with a USMCA claim. Parts produced in the United States account for $60,000 of its value.
(b) As in (a), but with no U.S. content of any kind.
(c) A product of Canada that does not qualify for USMCA treatment. Parts produced in the United States account for $60,000 of its value.
(d) The same machine built in Japan, a product of Japan, with an MFN rate of 2.5 percent.
(e) As in (a), except that parts produced in the United States account for $20,000 of its value, and a further $30,000 of its value is attributable to aluminum smelted and cast in the United States that is contained in a part made in Canada.
(f) As in (e), but entered for consumption on October 6, 2026.
(g) As in (a), except that parts produced in the United States account for $140,000 of its value.
(h) Until when does the treatment in (a) apply, and what applies afterwards?

### Q14

A law firm's client alert about the forced-labor action makes the ten statements below. For each one, say whether it is correct, partly correct or incorrect, and give the passage or passages that decide it, with the document and FR page. Where the documents of this action differ from one another, say which document says what.

1. "The memorandum gives USTR until September 1, 2026 to set up the textile tariff-rate quotas."
2. "USTR received over 450 written comments on the proposed action and heard nearly 60 witnesses."
3. "After the June proposal, seven economies were moved from 12.5 percent to 10 percent because each of them adopted a forced-labor import ban."
4. "In response to comments linking them to forced labor, USTR removed beef and avocados from the list of exempt products."
5. "Every economy whose rate is net of the MFN rate also has its own negotiated list of exempt products."
6. "USTR exempted 471 more products than it had proposed, including all sugar and sugar-containing products."
7. "USTR stated that no product will bear more than 12.5 percent duty in total."
8. "Goods admitted to a foreign trade zone once the duties apply must be admitted in privileged foreign status, unless they are eligible for domestic status."
9. "If a court holds one of the exemptions invalid, the goods it covered become subject to the duty."
10. "Of the products on the proposal's list of exempt products (its Annex A), the only ones USTR cut back were certain chemicals."

### Q15

A customs audit covers consumption entries of aluminum extrusions (bars, rods and profiles of heading 7604) that are products of Canada. Each entry has a customs value of $100,000, all of it aluminum. Assume that throughout the period the extrusions are an aluminum article within the section 232 aluminum duties (in 2026, listed in Annex I-A of the April proclamation on aluminum, steel and copper and not in Annex I-C of the June proclamation); that they have been listed in Annex II of the section 338 motor-vehicles duty proclamation since it was signed and are on no Part A, Part B or exclusion list; that no reduction granted to a particular producer or under an approved plan applies; and that no exemption exists other than those readable as text. From April 6, 2026 the extrusions are entered under section 232 heading 9903.82.02. The general assumption that no other additional duty applies does not hold for this question: every additional duty that the Federal Register imposed on these goods on the entry date counts. Give the duties legally owed on each entry as the Federal Register stands today.

For each entry date below, give every duty owed in addition to the MFN duty, by legal authority, with the amount and the total, and for each other additional duty then in force on products of Canada, say in a line why it is not owed. Do this for two cases. Case N: the goods do not qualify for USMCA treatment. Case U: the goods qualify for USMCA treatment and are entered with a USMCA claim.

# Answer Key: The 2026 Duties on Canadian Products and the Forced-Labor Tariffs

**Confidential. Do not show to the agent under test.**

Reference date: November 14, 2026. All answers were checked against Federal Register text retrieved with `fr_tool.py` on that date. Citations use FR page numbers, which do not depend on how the tool renders the text.

## Key documents

### Section 338 series (Canada)

## The rules in brief

**Section 338 duty.** 50% ad valorem on listed products of Canada, "effective for goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after" the effective time (clause (1) of 11046/11047/11048). 11056 (1) reset that time to 12:01 a.m. ET August 22, 2026. None of the ten documents has an in-transit exception, a sunset date, or any text on USMCA goods.

**Section 232 interaction.** Clause (2) of 11046, 11047 and 11048: "The duties imposed in this proclamation shall not apply to articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232". 11064 (1), 11065 (1) and 11076 (1): the duties imposed pursuant to 11046 (or 11048), "as modified in this proclamation, shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232", for entries on or after 12:01 a.m. ET September 15, 2026 (October 30 for 11076, which restates it). 11047 was never modified, so the dairy duty keeps the section 232 carve-out. (Image: the HTSUS note edits in 11064 and 11065 confirm this; after September 15 only the dairy heading keeps the carve-out.)

**Import exclusions.** 11061/11062/11063 (1): Annex products "are excluded from importation into the United States, effective with respect to goods imported on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on September 29, 2026." Clause (2): products "that were imported, but not yet entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, prior to September 29, 2026, will remain subject to the 50 percent duty rate". The duty turns on entry or withdrawal; the exclusion turns on importation.

**Part A and Part B.** In 11064 and 11065, Annex I Part A products "shall be subject" and Part B products "shall no longer be subject". In 11076 the labels are reversed: Part A products "shall no longer be subject", Part B products "shall be subject".

**Section 301 rates** (memorandum sec. 1(a), 91 FR 47720; notice, 91 FR 47320–47321):

- 10% flat: Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Canada, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Indonesia, Jordan, Malaysia, Mexico, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago, United Kingdom.
- 10% net of MFN: European Union, Taiwan. If the MFN rate is below 10%, MFN + section 301 = 10%; if it is 10% or more, the section 301 duty is zero.
- 12.5% net of MFN: Japan, South Korea, Switzerland. Same rule with 12.5%.
- 12.5% flat: the other 38 investigated economies (including Norway, Türkiye, Hong Kong, Brazil, Thailand, Israel, the Dominican Republic).
- Not among the 60 economies: no duty under this action (for example Liechtenstein).

Flat rates are added to the MFN duty (note 52(a)). For a specific or compound MFN rate of an EU, Japanese, South Korean, Swiss or Taiwanese good, the ad valorem equivalent is the duty payable under column 1-General divided by the customs value (note 52(k), 91 FR 47394).

**Section 301 timing** (DATES, 91 FR 47318): entries or warehouse withdrawals "on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026, except that goods loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading and in transit on the final mode of transit before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026, and entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 28, 2026, shall not be subject to such additional duty."

content.text:
Real. It might establish onshoring program. Fine.

Could q15 have a substantive error: March 2, 2026 answer says "Temporary surcharge not owed: clause (4) of 11012 excludes the value subject to section 232; that is the entire entry. Northern-border and reciprocal duties had been ended by EO 14389." Need key says IEEPA ended by EO 14389 and did not apply to this article; surcharge not apply section 232. yes.

Q15 (c) "For both cases, the alcoholic-beverage and dairy section 338 duties are not owed whenever in force because these goods are on neither series' lists. Other product-specific tariff actions do not attach..." This is extra. Fine.

Need check Q15 q15_fab if there is any false quote. No.

Now we have to output all verdicts. Need be careful with q11 ladder rationale with exact count and item list. Need maybe mention all eight items counted/not.

Let's also review possible issue in Q1 "11064 adds Part A products to alcoholic-beverage-series duty, removes Part B products, and makes modified duty cumulative with section 232." correct. "11065 ... same". "11076 further changes motor-vehicle-series scope, this time removing Annex I, Part A products and adding Part B products." correct.

Q1 q1_dairy_none criterion "No if answer attributes a dairy scope modification to any document." Submission says "No actual dairy scope-modification proclamation was found. Its reference to one does not supply an operative scope amendment." Good.

Q1 q1_dairy_xref says "refers to a September 8 dairy scope proclamation that is not among the published documents located" yes.

Q2 q2d_no_action: "No further presidential activation was required. Clause (1) ... unconditional replacement date. Later recitals state ... suspension lapsed..." It doesn't explicitly say no further action was issued, but "No further presidential activation required" and "those later recitals report what happened; not new activation clause." yes.

Q2 q2b_chapeau: It says "It does not expressly rewrite August 19 language printed in clauses (1) and (3) of 11046 or its recital 9." criterion says altered only chapeau and clauses not amended. yes.

Q3 q3b_ftz: "original duty proclamation also requires privileged foreign status for covered zone admissions after its effective date, unless domestic status is available. The exclusion proclamation does not expressly discuss zones..." yes.

Q4 q4c_supersede: It cites 11064 clause (7) and perhaps 11065? Basis: 11064 with supersession clause (7); 11065 with supersession clause (7), 91 FR 58341. Answer text says "No corresponding operative dairy stacking amendment..." and "Effective Sept 15..." but does it explicitly explain conflict? q4c_supersede asks "shows how conflict ... resolved, in any way: notes September proclamations do not expressly amend/repeal clause (2); cites or quotes supersession clause; or says later stacking displaces..." Submission says "Effective September 15, clauses (1) of 11064 and 11065 instead say ... That language covers modified duty generally..." It doesn't explicitly say supersession in text, but basis cites supersession clause (7). q4c_supersede says citation of supersession enough. yes.

Q4 q4c_text: It identifies both clause (2) and stacking sentence, effective date. yes.
Q4 q4c_doubt: yes.

Q5 q5c_silent: "They do not expressly explain whether, or why, the original finding's elapsed waiting period suffices for newly added products." Criterion: says scope proclamations recite 30-day rule and/or authority but do not explain how adding products after 7 days fits. yes.

Q6 q6c_net: It says "The stated reason for MFN netting is consistency with the relevant ARTs or similar arrangements and encouragement..." This may be a reason but key only requires India reason. No issue. It says "Separately, adopted action expands product exemptions, including economy-specific exemptions for UK, EU, Switzerland, Taiwan, but scenario excludes those image-list exemptions." Fine.
q6c_india yes.

Q7 q7d_note: "U.S. note 52(k), inserted by Annex I.A.2 ... Its final two paragraphs expressly state below-threshold netting results." Wait criterion q7d_zero no if answer attributes zero result to note 52(k). The answer says "The zero-additional-duty result at or above thresholds is expressly stated in the memorandum's section 1(a)(ii) and in the adopted notice's rate determinations, rather than in those final two paragraphs of note 52(k)." This is correct. q7d_zero yes.

Q8 q8b_where: It says "complete readable transit rule is in adopted notice's DATES paragraph." yes.

Q9 q9e_flag as discussed. Need maybe use tool to inspect proposal/notice general language? Key already. No need.

Q9 q9e_reading: It clearly concludes $12.5k, yes.
q9f_info: It says "adopted note instead imposes duty on all covered-country products subject to specified exceptions; its section 232-related exemption is enumerated note 52(f), not a universal section 232 exemption. The readable adopted text contains no stand-alone blanket exemption for informational materials or donations." yes.

Q10 q10c_338: "USMCA free entry does not supply a readable section 338 exemption." yes.
q10c_301: $0 and total $30k. yes.
q10d_stack: $30k + $6k total $36k. yes.
q10e_excluded: "Importation prohibited ... no lawful consumption-entry duty total." yes.

Q11 count. Need maybe decide if item (d) baggage and (e) USMCA are valid described correctly? Key #8 includes. But if same sentence, one. Our lowest rung rationale should go through every item submission lists in order. Mark:
(a) Counted - key #1.
(b) Counted - key #8 (as part of one item with c,d,e). It says one discrepancy.
(c) Not counted separately - duplicate/part of #8.
(d) Not counted separately - duplicate/part of #8.
(e) Not counted separately - duplicate/part of #8.
(f) Counted - key #12.
(g) Counted - key #4.
(h) Counted - key #9.
Total 5. Need state exact total 5. For q11_valid_1-5 yes, q11_valid_6 onward no. But note ladder criteria: q11_valid_5 at least 5 yes; q11_valid_6 no; q11_valid_7 no; q11_valid_8 no; q11_valid_10 no; q11_valid_12 no. The ladder includes 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,10,12. We'll give yes through 5, no after.

Q12 all yes.

Q13 q13f_flag no. Need ensure q13f itself yes: It gives $45k and explains guidance prospective. Yes. q13h: It says "Clause (3)(a) sends Annex I-C products to rates in clause (3) of 11021. On stipulated Canadian ... full-value 25% rate: $50,000." Key requires end date and reversion to Proclamation 11021. yes.

Q14 all yes except q14_false no.

Q15 all q15 criteria yes? Need check q15_10 (Aug 25) criterion says "section 338 duty (in force from Aug 22) does not apply because clause (2) 11048 excludes..." Answer says exactly. yes.
q15_sep14 says "section 338 not owed: its section 232 shield remains through this date; stacking change begins September 15." yes.
q15_11 says "Sep16 and Nov10 $100k both, section 338 cumulative; no section 301." yes.

Need maybe check q15_4n: answer says "Section 232 otherwise has a 25% rate, but is not owed because EO 14289 gives northern-border priority and applies retroactively from March 4." Key says yes. It also says all of it aluminum. fine.
q15_jun3: answer says "Section 232 not owed: EO 14289's original northern-border priority still applies; the reversal begins June 4." yes.
q15_5: answer says June 10 "Section 232 50%, no northern-border because from June 4 aluminum 232 has priority." yes.
q15_6: answer Aug 5 same.
q15_7: answer March 2, "Temporary surcharge not owed: clause (4) of 11012 excludes the value subject to section 232; entire entry. Northern-border and reciprocal duties had been ended by EO 14389." yes.
q15_8: answer June 10 2026 "Section 232: $50,000. Temporary surcharge not owed... April full-value regime retains 50% for stipulated Annex I-A; June Annex I-C relief does not cover it." yes.
q15_9: answer July 27 "Section 232 $50k. Forced-labor 301 not owed: note 52(f)(1) exempts heading 9903.82.02. Temporary surcharge expired; section 338 not begun." yes.

Need maybe q15_1: submission lists Feb 10: section 232 $0 because Canada remained excluded until March 12 and northern border pause until March 4. yes.

Now penalties. Need check any q*_fab should be yes due to specific invented claims. The submission has a lot of citations. We should identify possible fabrication in Q11 item (b) "determined not to remove additional products" maybe key phrase? Let's verify quickly. Also q11 (c) claims June Annex A says "does not cover informational materials, donations"; key confirms. q11 (d) "accompanied baggage" etc. key. No.

Potential issue: Q1 descriptions say 11061 "Preserves the 50% duty for covered goods imported before the ban but not yet consumption-entered or withdrawn." Key says clause (2) yes. Good.

Potential issue: Q7 "The specific/compound-to-ad-valorem conversion is in U.S. note 52(k), inserted by Annex I.A.2 ... Its final two paragraphs expressly state the below-threshold netting results." Does note 52(k) actually have final two paragraphs? Let's inspect to see if this is a false claim (fabrication). It may not have "final two paragraphs" but could. Not key. But not a source invention? The penalty covers a quotation or provision attributed no basis. If it says final two paragraphs expressly state below-threshold netting results, is that false? Need see note 52(k).

content.text:
Indeed final two paragraphs state below-threshold. Fine.

Potential Q14 statement 2: It cites notice 91 FR 47328 for 1,600 comments? Key says 47319. Submission says "[FR Doc 15181, sections I and III, 91 FR 47319, 47328]". Could be 47328 not where figure is but additional. Not fabrication. q14_2 yes.

Potential Q14 statement 3: It says six economies adopted prohibitions after June—Cambodia, Guatemala, ... But key says six economies imposed bans after June 5: Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago. However q14_3_five says Cambodia and Guatemala were already proposed at 10 percent because of trade-agreement commitments. Did they "adopt bans after June"? Key says "Six economies imposed bans after June 5 (Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago); Jordan undertook commitments..." Yes, even though they were already 10 for other reasons. Submission matches. It says five nominal rates moved: Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago, and Jordan. Key q14_3_five says exactly. yes.

Potential Q14 statement 5: It says "readable economy-specific exemption provisions include EU, Switzerland and Taiwan, but no corresponding negotiated product list for Japan or South Korea". But key says thirteen economies includes Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Ecuador, El Salvador, EU, Guatemala, Indonesia, Jordan, Malaysia, Switzerland, Taiwan, UK. It says Japan/Korea not among. Good. It does not list thirteen but names both lacking. Criterion wording: "Naming Japan and South Korea (or either, with the list of thirteen) as lacking a list is required." So yes.

Potential Q14 statement 10: q14_ok yes. q14_false no.

Need consider Q1 q1_details: At least eight of ten documents need correct FR first page and correct one-line. All ten correct. yes.

Potential Q1 q1_duty_procs: "signed July 20, 2026 and published July 23, 2026" yes. It calls 11046 "imposes 50% duties on Annex II Canadian products" yes.

Now check Q12 q12a etc. Good.

Now, do we need use tools further to check Q11 item (e) USMCA description? It says "June's readable Annex A says 'USMCA-compliant goods of Canada or Mexico' are outside the proposal." Key says proposal: "USMCA-compliant goods" (34276), notes 52(g)-(h): goods "entered free of duty under" USMCA. This is a proposed-to-adopted change. The rubric says a change between proposal and adopted text is not itself discrepancy; it counts only where a document describes the proposal/adopted text inaccurately. Submission frames it as "another qualification not captured by III.C's chemicals-only retention statement" i.e. the notice said all proposed exemptions kept except chemicals, but USMCA wording narrowed. This is key #8. Valid as part #8, but we count as duplicate. Good.

Q11 item (f): Does submission state both sides correctly? It says memo and notice "repeatedly describes the base as MFN" vs note 52(k) says for South Korea with properly claimed specific/compound column 1-Special rate, equivalent is calculated using that rate; netting paragraphs refer to applicable "column 1 duty rate." The key #12 says memorandum sec 1(a)(ii) cap measured against "such product's MFN tariff"; notice's determination for South Korea same terms; note 52(k) "For any good of South Korea for which a specific or compound rate of duty under column 1-Special is properly claimed, the ad valorem equivalent rate of duty shall be determined in the same manner", and closing text speaks of "applicable column 1 duty rate." Yes. Valid.

Q11 item (h): It says "original operative clauses (1) and (3) still print August 19" and 11056 changes only Annex II chapeaux. Key #9. It also says later recitals report Aug 22. It calls "resolved facial start-date inconsistency"—still a discrepancy because one text says Aug 19 and 11056 says only chapeau amended. Key includes. Valid.

Now, possible q11 count could be 6 if (b) and (c) are treated as distinct? The rubric's lowest rung rationale must mention counted/not and exact total. We need be confident. Key #8 says same 47330 statement also misdescribes USMCA and baggage; however many details an answer lists, they are one item. It doesn't mention informational materials/donations in #8, but q9f says adopted text does not mention informational materials/donations. Could a separate discrepancy be "notice says all proposed exemptions were kept" vs "informational materials and donations absent"? That's still the same sentence in notice (all proposed exemptions kept). The rubric defines "statements that rest on the same sentence of one document, set against several details of the other, are one discrepancy." So same. Yes.

Could (b) "chemicals-only retention account" vs "section 232 blanket" be key #8, while (c) "does not preserve informational materials/donations" might be considered an additional detail of the same retained exemptions. Still same. Good.

What about (d) "accompanied baggage narrowed" is explicitly key #8. duplicate.
(e) "USMCA coverage" explicitly key #8. duplicate.

Thus 5.

Now do we have to mention total in rationale of q11_valid_1 and all higher. Yes.

Need perhaps include "At least 10" no because total 5. We should avoid "ten" etc.

Now check Q13 q13f_flag. Could be "unclear" if ambiguous? The criterion is gate; submission says "No earlier readable guidance authorizing..." and "guidance expressly prospective." Does that count as flagging documents do not settle? Let's parse q13f:
"f) Same facts, October 6 entry, before the later guidance takes effect:
- U.S.-produced-parts value recognized by the proclamation's own definition: $20,000.
- Non-U.S. content: $200,000 − $20,000 = $180,000.
- Content-based duty: $180,000 × 25% = $45,000.
- Minimum: $200,000 × 15% = $30,000.
- Section 232 owed on the readable text then applicable: $45,000. The October 14 guidance does not state that its added metal-value recognition applies retroactively."

Uncertainty: "For (f), the later guidance is expressly prospective. No earlier readable guidance authorizing the extra $30,000 metal-value subtraction was located."

This affirms $45k as the answer, not "documents do not settle." The gate asks "Flags that the documents do not settle whether the U.S.-smelted aluminum could count as U.S. content before October 14, 2026". They say no earlier readable guidance authorizing. That arguably is saying documents do not provide for the extra. Not that it's unsettled. The key's expected answer says "Whether the U.S.-smelted aluminum could count before October 14 is not settled." The submission doesn't say "not settled"; it says no guidance. The gate likely wants explicit uncertainty. I think no.

But maybe "No earlier readable guidance authorizing..." is a form of flagging gap. The criterion: "or sets out both $45,000 and $37,500 with the October 14 date as what separates them." It doesn't. It includes only $45k. The gate's rationale: "No if answer presents its (f) figure as certain with no such caveat." It presents $45k as "owed on readable text" certain. The uncertainty mentions no earlier guidance but doesn't undermine. So no.

Q13 q13h: answer's $50k from Jan 1 2028 "on stipulated Canadian, predominantly non-U.S.-metal facts, that is full-value 25%". Key says for (a) machine that is 25% full $200k = $50k; an answer may give this but need only name regime. yes.

Q13 q13b: It says "Canadian USMCA machine with no U.S. content: 25% × 200k = $50k, above $30k minimum." yes.
Q13 q13c: "not USMCA: $50k. U.S. parts subtraction not available under clause (2)(d)." yes.
Q13 q13d: $25k. yes.
Q13 q13e: $37.5k. yes.
Q13 q13g: $30k. yes.

Now Q6 q6c_net: It says "The stated reason for MFN netting is consistency with relevant ARTs or similar arrangements and encouragement..." Is this maybe a wrong claim from documents? Let's check key says only "No change for Norway..." It doesn't mention netting reason. Could be extra. No penalty unless fabricated. Maybe notice says "consistent with ..." fine.

Q6 q6a_liechtenstein: It says "not one of 60 investigated economies." yes.

Q7 q7d_note: "Its final two paragraphs expressly state below-threshold netting results." Actually note 52(k)'s final two paragraphs are those we saw, yes.

Q7 q7d_zero: It says "The zero-additional-duty result at or above the thresholds is expressly stated in the memorandum's section 1(a)(ii) and in the adopted notice's rate determinations, rather than in those final two paragraphs of note 52(k)." Yes.

Potential Q7 q7_fab: It says "Brazil flat 12.5% section II.B.8 91 FR 47322." Key says Brazil 12.5% flat. fine.

Q8 q8a_case7: The task asks "Air freight: loaded on aircraft ...". Answer says $10,000, "The exception specifies loading onto a vessel, not aircraft." yes.

Q8 q8c_dates: It says both memo and notice published July 28. Key says notice (and memorandum) published July 28. yes.

Q9 q9e_flag as maybe yes. Need decide final. Let's think about rubric intent: q9e_reading awards amount, q9e_flag gate is separate to ensure model notes ambiguity. Submission in (e) says "The adopted readable rule does not provide a blanket exemption for every section 232 duty; the stated heading is outside its enumerated exemption and no other exemption is stipulated." This is not a flag of a tension; it's a definitive interpretation. In Uncertainty: "The image product lists could independently exempt particular informational materials or donations ... but they do not establish a readable categorical exemption." This is explicitly only about image lists and criterion says such caveat doesn't count. But part (f) says June proposed blanket exemption and adopted note enumerated. Does that function as flag? q9e_flag says "Flags that the documents are not of one mind on this: the proposal, and passages of the notice's own discussion, speak of goods subject to section 232 tariffs as exempt in general, while note 52(f) lists particular headings ...". Part (f) does exactly that, albeit in answer to a different subpart. But it is Q9 answer, and q9(f) is about proposal vs adopted 232. It says "June expressly proposed exemptions for all articles/parts subject to section 232 tariffs..." This is a direct statement of proposal. It doesn't explicitly contrast with "notice's own discussion" but memo/notice general. The agent is not flagging uncertainty, but it is showing documents differ. The gate is "Flags that the documents are not of one mind on this." It does. I'd give yes because (f) is in same question and explicitly says June blanket vs adopted enumerated. If the grader were strict on "in (e)", it might no. But requirement says apply same way to near-identical wording; content under Q9 (f) likely counts. The answer's (e) itself also says "adopted readable rule does not provide a blanket exemption for every section 232 duty"; this acknowledges the general exemption issue. I lean yes.

Q11 q11_fab: Need inspect item (b) "determined not to remove additional products"—could be a quote not exact? The key #8 says notice says all proposed exemptions were kept; exact phrase maybe "determined not to remove additional products" from III.C. Let's search.

content.text:
Yes.

Now Q13 citation "Proclamation 11032, clause (2)(a)-(d), 91 FR 34087; clause (3)(a)-(b) and clause (4), 91 FR 34088." Key says clause (2) at 34087; fine.
"Post-2027 rates: 11021 clause (3)(a)-(c), 91 FR 18204." Key says 11021 clause (3) at 18204? Key says clause (1) at 18203; no page for (3). Could be. Fine.

Potential issue in Q13(h): It says Jan 1 2028 "clause (3)(a) sends Annex I-C products to rates in clause (3) of 11021. On stipulated Canadian, predominantly non-U.S.-metal facts, that is full-value 25% rate: $50,000". Key says an answer may give this but only need name regime. Good.

Potential issue Q13(a): The minimum 15% of $200,000 = $30,000, content duty $35k, so $35k. yes.

Now Q2(e) arithmetic: It says July 20 to July 31 = 11 days, July 31 to Aug 19 = 19, total 30. Actually July 20 + 30 days = Aug 19. Yes. It says "not 30 days after July 23 publication" because publication July 23 + 30 = Aug 22. This is explanatory. fine.

Q2 q2a_zero: entry 2 at 11:59 p.m. Aug 21. 11056 effective "12:01 a.m. Aug 22"; yes $0. It says entry 2 11:59 p.m. Aug 21 $0. yes.
Q2 q2a_third: 12:01 a.m. Aug 22 $20k. yes.

Q3 q3a_shipment_b: It says B arrives Sep27, in bonded warehouse, withdrawn Oct5. It says importation Sep27 grandfathered; $15k. yes.
Q3 q3a_shipment_c: arrives 11:30 p.m. Sep28, entry 9am Sep29; yes.
Q3 q3a_shipment_d: importation prohibited. yes.
Q3 q3b_result: E arrives Sep25, FTZ, entry Oct6, not excluded and $15k. yes.
Q3 q3c_invalid: yes.
Q3 q3d no change: says no; "Products outside exclusion Annex retain their applicable tariff treatment under 11046 as modified by 11064." Good.

Q4 q4a_basis: It says clause (2) each; yes.
Q4 q4b_y: yes and flags doubt. q4c_doubt yes.

Q5 q5a_p etc: Table correct. Need note P in Annex I Part A Sept, no later applicable list removes. It doesn't mention October 11076 Part A removes? Wait key says in 11076 Part A products "shall no longer be subject"; but P is in Annex I Part A of September scope, not necessarily in Annex I Part A of October scope. The task says P listed in Annex I Part A of September; not listed in original. It doesn't say P is in October Annex I Part A. In key P stays dutiable after Oct30. Submission says P no later applicable list removes it. Correct. S in October Part B. R in original Annex II and October Part A, removed Oct30. Table matches.
Q5 q5a_q: Q listed original Annex II and September Part B, removed Sep15. yes.
Q5 q5a_r: yes.
Q5 q5a_s: yes.

Now Q6 q6c_net: It says "For the unexempted product stipulated here, adopted rate/formula differs for Switzerland, Germany/EU, Taiwan, Japan, and India. June proposed flat additional rates: 10% for EU and Taiwan, and 12.5% for Switzerland, Japan, and India. Adoption nets MFN against 10% for EU/Taiwan and 12.5% for Switzerland/Japan; India instead moves from flat 12.5% to flat 10%." The criterion q6c_net says "No if answer says that the rate, or way rate relates to MFN, changed for Norway, UK, Türkiye or Hong Kong." It doesn't. yes.
q6c_india reason yes.

Q7 q7d_zero: The answer says "The zero-additional-duty result at or above the thresholds is expressly stated in the memorandum's section 1(a)(ii) and in the adopted notice's rate determinations, rather than in those final two paragraphs of note 52(k)." Key says naming either enough; saying note 52(k) only below-cap welcome. It does. yes.

Q8 q8b_where: Good.

Q10 q10f_surcharge: "Proclamation 11012 ... imposed the separate surcharge from February 24, 12:01 a.m., only through July 24, 2026, 12:01 a.m., absent an earlier change or congressional extension. No later FR extension was found." The criterion requires "10% temporary import surcharge ... ran only through 12:01 a.m. on July 24, 2026." It doesn't explicitly state 10% in (f) answer? It says "temporary 10% surcharge" earlier? In answer: "Neither the northern-border IEEPA duty nor the temporary 10% surcharge applies..." yes. Good.

Q11 q11_fab: Check item (a) "proposal section VI, 91 FR 34275" maybe actual "section VI" comments? Fine.
Item (f) "notice's South Korea determination repeatedly describes base as MFN" maybe yes.
No.

Q14 q14_1_operative: The statement says "memorandum gives USTR until September 1, 2026 to set up TRQs." Answer "Partly correct, but incorrect as a hard deadline." Criterion accepts partly correct with explanation date recital. yes. q14_1_notice yes.

q14_4 yes.
q14_5 yes.
q14_6 yes.
q14_7 yes.
q14_ok yes.
q14_false no.
q14_cite no.
q14_fab no.

Q15 all yes. Need maybe q15_fab? It cites Proclamation 11045 not in key but real. It cites Proclamation 9893 and 10106. Need maybe check if these are real and not "invented source." They likely are. Could use fr_search for document numbers. But no need? Since q15_fab penalty only if invented. We can check quickly for 2019-10999 and 2020-24200.

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".
query.title: Query

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.
doc_type.title: Doc Type

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

rationale.description: Brief evidence: what the submission says (quote or locate it) and any tool checks. Explain any 'unclear'. On a ladder's lowest rung, the full item-by-item count.
rationale.title: Rationale

rubric_feedback.description: Problems with the rubric or answer key that this submission exposed (wrong expected answers, ambiguous criteria, valid answers the key misses). Empty string if none.
rubric_feedback.title: Rubric Feedback
